chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed while he was a traveler, so he completed the prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was within the [prescribed] time, let him repeat [the prayer]; and if the time has passed, then no [need to repeat].'

key_terms.الْوَقْت: time (the prescribed period for a specific prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler prays four rak'ahs instead of two?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of a traveler's mistaken full prayer depends on whether the specific prayer time remains active; if the time is still within bounds, the error necessitates repetition as a shortened prayer, whereas if the time has expired, the full prayer stands as valid. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the 'time of the prayer' (waqt) serves as the critical boundary for determining whether a structural error requires correction or is excused by the passage of time. It underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding travel, prioritizing the actual performance within the designated window over strict adherence to the shortened form if the time constraint has already passed.
